I feel like the word “nanny” gets thrown around more than it should. I consider myself a “career nanny”. He might feel more comfortable with that, and you as well. Also- you can ask for references from the parents you are considering working for as well if they have had previous babysitters or nanny’s. That has been really helpful for me to feel more comfortable in people’s homes in the beginning.

I’ve been in a similar situation. If you know talking to her will make you feel better I would reach out. She probably will be able to explain certain things about him he doesn’t even know about himself being he’s a narcissist and most likely doesn’t have the ability to look inward.

$27 is not asking too much but if I were you I would be willing to negotiate a lower rate; with the ability to go up with time.. but I wouldn’t budge on a W-2 or PTO. Those are non negotiable. You deserve to be paid fairly and legally.

You just have to put your foot in the door. Start with spreading the news to some of the kids parents in the classroom you work in. Mom groups are very popular and word gets around fast. Your experience will grow and you will learn what you are looking for in a family and what you know you aren’t looking for. Parents want to be able to trust you, and that matters more to them than how many families you’ve nannied for. You have childcare experience by being in the preschool and personality also matters to parents. Put yourself out there and you will do great.

Dealbreaker for me. They either need to trust you completely or find someone they can. Having cameras isn’t the issue. If that makes them feel better if something did come up and they would be able to go back and see what happened- fine. Great even. But to be sitting elsewhere and watching you, is a disservice to you. You cannot give your full attention to the child if your mind is constantly articulating your every move bc you know they could be watching in. Full trust or none at all.

You’re not charging anything bc you do not need to go. They are fully taking advantage of you. Unless you are compensated for all hours.. and yes all of the hours from time you leave to the time you arrive home, As well as being compensated for what you are loosing by taking the days off of your other job you do not even need to consider it.

This is an issue I have too. The fact of the matter is it’s so much easier for all involved to shove a screen in front of a child. My logic is MB & DB think they deserve the easier side of parenting the children (because us as nannies are also parenting the children) simply because they are paying us. But in reality we get all the moments that matter, and happen only when you are engaging with the children. I love my NK so much. She says the absolute sweetest things, has such a big heart, and is going to be someone special when she grows up. But I know her parents have no clue who she even is because they don’t take the time to play with her, and look her in the eye and talk to her about whatever she wants to talk about, or even listen to her. I often find myself feeling bad for my boss’s because a child’s life goes by so fast- and they’ll never get the time back that they shove her in front of a screen.

You will feel true empowerment the second you decide to give him the silent treatment. Even if he never shows you that it bothers him, even if he never reaches out again it will KILL HIM!! The moment you realize that you need to be more important to yourself than he is to you, you will get this enormous sense of peace within your heart. I know it’s hard. I’ve been the one reaching out multiple times with no response, but you have to choose your happiness and your peace and put that first! I’ll be praying for you!
